balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For NRG Energy, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
NRG reports four segments: Texas (ERCOT generation and retail), East (PJM/other regulated-market generation and retail), West/Other (the balance of the generation fleet, including the LS Power plants added when that deal closed 2026-01-30) and Vivint (retail smart-home subscriptions).

For NRG Energy, Inc.: East overtook Texas as the largest segment by revenue in FY2025 and again in Q1 2026 -- read that against the generation-capacity chart below, since it is the LS Power acquisition showing up in the mix, not organic Texas growth slowing.

What to watch:

  • Whether West/Other revenue scales with the roughly doubled generation capacity
  • Vivint's small but steady contribution versus the much larger, more volatile power segments

segmentOperatingIncome.title: Segment operating income
segmentOperatingIncome.content:
Operating income by the same four segments. Unlike revenue, a merchant-generation segment's operating income swings with wholesale power prices and hedging outcomes quarter to quarter, so a single quarter's loss is not necessarily a trend.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: East posted a roughly $346m operating loss in Q2 2025, before the LS Power plants were folded in -- the chart is the way to see whether the enlarged, more diversified generation base smooths that volatility going forward.

What to watch:

  • Whether any one segment's losses are recurring or a single bad quarter (commodity/hedge timing)
  • Vivint's margin versus the power segments -- a steadier, subscription-like income stream

generationFleet.title: Generation capacity and volume
generationFleet.content:
Generation capacity (MW) is the nameplate size of the owned fleet at period end; generation volume (GWh) is what was actually produced and sold, split by segment.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: capacity was flat near 13,000 MW for FY2023-FY2025, then roughly doubled once the LS Power acquisition closed on 2026-01-30 -- this chart is the direct read on whether that bought capacity is being utilised, not just owned. Generation volume and the segment detail are disclosed annually, so most of the history here is FY-only; capacity itself is also reported intra-year once the deal closed.

What to watch:

  • Volume growing in proportion to the new capacity (utilisation), not just the MW figure
  • Which segment absorbs the new plants -- it shows up as West/Other here

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For NRG Energy, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
